architecture.reframe: writeup section 1: 'the true entropy isn't the video itself, but the expected outputs of the evaluation models... The answer itself is the true entropy.' Independent public discovery of the evaluator-equivalent-witness paradigm.

adversarial_existence_proof.claim: direct gradient descent on INPUT PIXELS against the frozen evaluators (Adam + Huber, C&W margin, per-dim normalized PoseNet outputs) reached SegNet 100% agreement (d_seg 0.00) + PoseNet MSE < 1e-9 in 2h on one T4
adversarial_existence_proof.status: [external claim, THEIR measurement — not verified on our apparatus]
adversarial_existence_proof.why_abandoned: storing per-pixel adversarial frames busts rate; generating them at inflate time would require scorer weights in-archive (the same rule-118 compliance wall we codified)

master_renderer.name: TokenRendererV62
master_renderer.role: frame_1 (odd index) — carries the SegNet decision state
master_renderer.input: one-hot(5 classes) on the 384x512 SegNet input grid
master_renderer.body: 3-layer 3x3 stride-1 CNN (32ch, GroupNorm, GELU) + per-pair FiLM (600x8 embedding -> 64) -> sigmoid*255 -> bilinear up to 874x1164
master_renderer.receptive_field_claim: EXACTLY 7 by derivation (writeup 7.2): SegNet's boundary decision localizes to stem (stride-2 3x3) + Stage-0 depthwise 3x3 => a 7-input-pixel window; 3 layers is the unique depth matching it (RF 5 under-covers, RF 9 wastes capacity the metric cannot see)
master_renderer.receptive_field_status: [THEIR derivation + working existence proof — FROZEN-SPACE CANDIDATE, not our measurement]
master_renderer.determinism_engineering: bake_film_table() computes the FiLM table on CPU FP32 because cuBLAS tiny-matmul kernels differ Ada vs Turing

slave_renderer.name: ShrinkSingleNeRV
slave_renderer.role: frame_0 — pose duty only; SegNet never sees it
slave_renderer.body: 6-float per-pair latent -> Linear stem -> 5x (depthwise 3x3 + 1x1 + PixelShuffle) -> per-pair RGB bias; LSQ+ INT4 throughout; NO FiLM, NO skips (deliberate: the latent already carries frame identity)
slave_renderer.superseded_by: PR130's 23,054 B neutral-gray low-rank carrier at d_pose 2.331e-5 — 19.6x better d_pose at 9,233 FEWER bytes

token_coder.two_level_partition: 12x16 = 192 independent P=32 patches (cross-frame conditioned via prev-frame tokens conv_past + CausalSPM cross-patch summary) x group order s = c + delta*r (delta=2)
token_coder.parallelism_gain: 94 sequential group steps per frame instead of 196,608 raster steps (~2000x fewer); T4 end-to-end decode ~18 min

architecture.weight_compression: SCN (Self-Compressing Networks): learnable per-layer bit budget IN the loss — the optimizer allocates quantization precision; + PPMd over the quantized state-dict bytes (~2x further)

failed_variants_worth_remembering.name: HPAC residual-prediction direction
failed_variants_worth_remembering.what: factorize as p(class-diff | prev frame) instead of p(class | spatial ctx, prev frame)
failed_variants_worth_remembering.lesson: for temporal grammars: condition on the past, do NOT code the label-diff

gt_decode_custody_incident.what: pre-DALI phases trained against PyAV-decoded GT
gt_decode_custody_incident.measured_gap: train-set d_seg 0.000035 vs evaluator 0.000712 — 20x, from NVDEC vs PyAV chroma/color conversion
gt_decode_custody_incident.resolution: shipped checkpoint required a DALI-corrected fine-tune
gt_decode_custody_incident.significance: their independent instance of our GT-decode custody law (frame_utils.yuv420_to_rgb only)

engineering_stack.archive_grammar: 5 separate STORED ZIP members (tokens.bin, slave.pt.gz, master.pt.gz, hpac.pt.ppmd, meta.pt)
engineering_stack.member_overhead_cost: 506 B vs PR130's 100 B single-member — 406 B lost purely to member count. Independent measured confirmation of our L20 monolithic-archive lesson.
engineering_stack.hpac_decode_device: FORCED TO CPU — comment: different GPUs (encoder RTX 4090, eval T4) produce slightly different FP32 softmax -> arithmetic decoder asserts. CPU FP32 is portable.
engineering_stack.determinism_approach: pin the non-portable ops to CPU FP32 (both the FiLM table and the whole HPAC decode). PR130 replaced this with an integer lattice — a strictly stronger fix that also removes the CPU-speed penalty.
